decision: The merged per-bundle Contract and Offer permission lists become per-bundle checks: Contract read is held through the Contract Preparer or Contract Approver grant, source Offer read through the Offer Preparer or Offer Approver grant, pricing snapshot read through the Pricing User or Offer Preparer grant (apps/web/src/contract/contract-grants.ts); preparation, project linking and model selection come from the Preparer, approval and signature recording from the Approver, early preparation from Early Preparation; remount and authority keys carry the grants their per-bundle fields carried
why: The registry gives each permission to exactly these bundles, so each merged-list check holds for the same registry-consistent actors; Contract commands send no captured assignment or version (bodies carry revisions and values only)

decision: A Contract fixture that read Offers without pricing snapshots takes the Offer Approver grant; one with approval permissions takes the Contract Approver v1 grant and loses the Preparer grant when it had no preparation; a missing Commercial Intake or Client assignment takes v1 with a synthetic id; a Project read takes the captured version (v2 adds project.create)
why: The Offer Approver is the only registry bundle with the Offer read and no snapshot read, which keeps the direct-preparation form hidden as before; approval always brings signature recording in the registry

decision: The Contract reader without preparation or approval keeps a Contract Preparer grant narrowed by hand to the Contract read in component tests; the mocked browser reader, whose Actor the parser would refuse (#1332), becomes a preparer of a superseded Version, which offers neither Run nor Decision
why: No registry version confers the Contract read alone; the component tests keep the no-Run and history assertions on the narrowed grant, the browser journey keeps them on a state the registry can produce

decision: An unknown captured Contract Approver version is asserted as a refusal of the whole current Actor through readCurrentActor instead of a component-only denial
why: The current Actor parser refuses an unknown grant for the whole Actor (#1332), as #1381 did for Internal Tasks

decision: Shared fixtures (model Contract, reported signing, Contract localization, Activity localization, invoice record) keep their per-bundle Contract, Offer, Client, Intake and Document fields beside the new grants
why: Commercial intake, Offer, commercial PDF, invoice record authority and Documents still read them until their areas migrate
